sections.heading: A one-shot debut
sections.text: One submission was enough to rattle the leading pack. The recorded submission timestamp and the first observed public score were more than a day apart; the observations do not reveal its processing time. It stormed into the top ten on arrival, then slipped outside it by the dated observation below. The newcomer is a Competitions Grandmaster based in Kyoto, Japan, and was near the very top of Kaggle’s overall competition rankings when the reporter checked on 2 November.

sections.heading: Franzen’s other front
sections.text: Daniel Franzen is fighting on another front. Alongside his ARC-3 work with The ARChitects, he plays ARC-2 alone—and his solo entry has made a major climb. The dated table shows the move.

sections.heading: The infinity pair, here as Progress
sections.text: The infinity pair is making noise here too. Van-Phuc Huynh and Trần M. Tiến play ARC-2 as Progress, and they have hauled that entry sharply upward as well.

sections.heading: Big climbs further down
sections.text: Hack2Publish delivered the biggest score gain in the table. KaggleARC and AndreasToescher also surged. Nearer the leaders, ibyyue climbed onto the gold cutoff. The pack is not waiting politely for the bell.

sections.heading: The top six held
sections.text: The leading group held across the comparison window. Tufa Labs remains ahead of Yi-Chia Chen, with nvbanana and Domdolus Tolus behind them. ARC Mutants, the editor’s ARC-2 team, also improved. Exact standings belong in the dated table below.

sections.heading: The private-board reckoning
sections.text: The published submission deadline is 2 November at 23:59 UTC. A public reading cannot tell us whether every submitted run has finished scoring. Medals are decided on the private leaderboard. One shot has already rattled the ledges. Where will this newcomer land when the private scores arrive?
